newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Goh expects election win before vote.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Goh expects election win before vote.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said on Sunday he expected his People's Action Party (PAP) to win general elections before he announces a date for the vote, Singapore Television reported.

It quoted Goh as saying he did not expect opposition parties to be able to put up more than 40 candidates for the 83 elected seats in parliament, which would mean the PAP winning a majority before voting.
The same thing happened in the last elections in 1991.
On Saturday, Goh told reporters he would name the date for the elections on Monday, the last day for the nomination of candidates. Most analysts expect the vote to be called for early January.
The PAP is widely expected to win all but a few seats. In the parliament dissolved last Monday, the opposition held only four seats.
Opposition parties have difficulty persuading people to stand against the monolithic PAP, which has transformed Singapore into a thriving city-state.
They complain that the government has all sorts of ways to make their lives difficult.

Last week, The New Paper told the story of Christopher Neo telling his fiancee three months before their wedding he was quitting his job because he had just been elected assistant treasurer of the National Solidarity Party (NSP).
It said Neo did not want to make difficulties for his firm "as it dealt with official organisations".
The PAP, which also sues opposition politicians over any perceived infraction, makes no apologies for doing what it can to keep the opposition out of parliament.
"Do you think we could have done even half of what was achieved in the last 30 years if we had a multi-party system and a revolving-door government?" Goh asked university students on Friday.
"Do you think we could have done just as well if we had a government which was constantly being held in check by 10 to 20 opposition members in the last 30 years?"
